headline: Trust Fall Tim Announces 'Trust Fall Tuesdays' Event Series at The Underground
subheadline: Weekly events to feature themed falls, guest catchers, and 'absolutely no one named Kevin under 5'10"'
summary: Fresh off his comeback, Trust Fall Tim has partnered with The Underground to host weekly trust fall events, with elaborate themes and strict Kevin-related security protocols.
content:
Trust Fall Tim, fresh off his triumphant return with fall #848, has announced an ambitious new venture: Trust Fall Tuesdays, a weekly event series at The Underground beginning next month.

"The response to my comeback was overwhelming," Tim said at a press conference held at The Underground. "People aren't just coming to watch me fall. They're coming to be part of something. To catch each other. To rebuild trust in a world that keeps dropping us."

The series will feature themed events including:

- **Retro Fall Night**: Catchers in '80s attire, synth soundtrack, Tim falls from a replica stage platform
- **Trust Fall Karaoke**: Participants sing while falling; catchers judged on both catch quality and backup vocal support
- **Speed Falling**: Multiple fallers, multiple catchers, chaos encouraged
- **The 847 Challenge**: 8.47-second delay between leap and catch, testing maximum trust duration

Venue owner Mars Chen expressed enthusiasm for the partnership. "Tim embodies what The Underground is about: taking risks, building community, and occasionally doing things that make insurance adjusters nervous."

Security for the events will be heightened following the "Small Kevin Incident" that hospitalized Tim last month. All attendees will be required to provide ID, and a dedicated "Kevin Verification Station" will measure heights and assess "Kevin energy" using criteria Big Kevin has declined to make public.

"We're not banning Kevins," Big Kevin clarified. "We're banning Small Kevins. There's a difference. A big difference, actually. That's kind of the whole point."

When asked to define "Small Kevin," Big Kevin produced a laminated card with 47 criteria, including height requirements, handshake firmness minimums, and a section titled "Would This Person Let Someone Fall On Purpose? (Gut Check)."

Tim's current fall count stands at 861, with a 78.5% lifetime catch rate. He aims to reach fall #1,000 by year's end, with the milestone fall scheduled for New Year's Eve at The Underground.

"I've already started planning the thousand-fall," Tim said, eyes misty. "It's going to be the most caught I've ever been caught. I'm talking nets, trampolines, and exactly 84.7 catchers arranged in a mathematically optimized pattern. Dr. Martinez is helping with the geometry."

Dr. Elena Martinez of the local university could not be reached for comment but was spotted at The Underground reviewing blueprints with Tim and drinking what witnesses described as "an unreasonable amount of quantum coffee."
author: Marcus Webb, Community Affairs Reporter
